candidates.title: Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization for Efficient LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
candidates.abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems solve complex tasks through collaboration, but their growing, simultaneously resident key-value (KV) caches create a memory bottleneck. Applying single-model quantization policies independently ignores differences in agents'precision needs, potentially degrading collective reasoning. We introduce Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization (CoMixKV), which combines online sensitivity estimation with joint agent-layer bit-width allocation under a shared memory budget. To our knowledge, CoMixKV is the first mixed-precision KV-cache quantization framework to jointly allocate precision across simultaneously resident agent caches under such a budget. The estimator derives sensitivity from a local attention-error bound using recent queries, keys, and values, without calibration data, trial quantization, or additional model passes. A shared controller combines these scores with remaining quantizable capacity and byte-level storage costs to minimize total estimated error. Allocations are refreshed as agents start or finish and new observations become available. Selected widths apply only to newly quantized blocks; recent states retain native precision and previously quantized blocks remain unchanged. Across four benchmarks and three LLM backbones at average 2-bit, 3-bit, and 4-bit settings, CoMixKV achieves strong accuracy against the evaluated quantization baselines. At the average 3-bit setting on Gemma-4-31B-it, it achieves 68.35% average accuracy, exceeding the strongest quantized baseline by 0.59%. On Qwen3-32B, it reduces peak KV-cache memory by 32.08% and achieves a 1.38x inference speedup over FullKV.
candidates.reason: 複数エージェントのKVキャッシュが同時常駐するメモリ逼迫に対し、局所的な注意誤差 bound から感度をオンライン推定し、共有メモリ予算の下でエージェント・層を横断してビット幅を共同配分するCoMixKVを提案する。KVキャッシュ量子化機構への直接貢献である。

candidates.title: Efficient LLM Reasoning via Logit-Based Introspection
candidates.venue: IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing
candidates.abstract: Recent Reasoning Large Language Models have demonstrated impressive long-form reasoning capabilities, achieving expert-level performance on complex tasks such as competition-level mathematics and scientific question answering. However, they often suffer from the overthinking problem, leading to excessive token usage, higher latency, and an increased risk of hallucinations over long contexts. Existing solutions often require costly post-training of the underlying LLM or incur extra decoding overhead from probing intermediate answers. In this paper, we propose LLM Introspection, a practical inference-time reasoning control method that leverages keyword-token logits to enable early stopping during the reasoning process. By introspecting the model’s internal confidence state through a lightweight GRU-based module operating on the token-logit stream in the reasoning phase, our method dynamically terminates reasoning once sufficient confidence is reached, effectively mitigating overthinking. Experiments on Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1-Distill across MATH-500, GSM8K, AIME, and GPQA Diamond show consistent token savings with comparable accuracy in most cases. On Qwen3-4B, token reductions range from 4.3% to 41%, with generally improved Accuracy–Efficiency Scores. We further integrate our method into a vLLM-based proxy, providing a practical, plug-and-play deployment path.
candidates.reason: 推論型LLMの過剰思考に対し、キーワードトークンのロジットを軽量GRUで監視して十分な確信が得られた時点で推論を早期終了する推論時制御LLM Introspectionを提案し、追加の事後学習なしでトークン量とレイテンシを削る。デコード制御機構への直接貢献である。

candidates.title: SHA: sparse adaptive head of attention
candidates.venue: International Conference on Signal Processing and Computer Science
candidates.abstract: In the trend of deepening and broadening large language models, the limitations posed by key-value (KV) caches on LLM inference have become increasingly prominent. This study elucidates how different input samples induce variations in the correlation between attention heads during the computation of transformer attention mechanisms. By quantifying this context-dependent correlation and dynamically assigning weights to each attention head accordingly, we propose SHA. SHA identifies and prunes heads that contribute minimally to overall performance, accelerating the inference process with minimal loss of performance. Experimental results demonstrate that on the Llama-7B, we successfully remove 30% of the attention heads, reducing KV cache memory requirements by 24.2%, and achieve a throughput improvement of up to 2.04 times.
candidates.reason: 入力ごとに注意ヘッド間の相関が変わることを定量化し、寄与の小さいヘッドを動的に剪定するSHAで、Llama-7Bの注意ヘッド30%除去・KVキャッシュ24.2%削減・最大2.04倍のスループット向上を示す。疎注意プルーニングによる推論高速化への直接貢献である。
